Right now, its Wired Doorbell Pro is down to $199 ($50 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , while the Battery Doorbell Plus is on sale for $119.99 ($60 off) at Amazon and Best Buy . Both deals are the second-best prices we’ve seen, just $20 shy of their Prime Day lows. Ring Wired Doorbell Pro Where to Buy: $249.99 $199.99 at Amazon $249.99 $199.99 at Best Buy $249.99 $199.99 at Ring Ring Battery Doorbell Plus (second-gen) Where to Buy: $179.99 $119.99 at Amazon (includes Indoor Cam Plus) $179.99 $119.99 at Best Buy $179.99 $119.99 at Ring Aside from how they’re powered, the main difference between the two comes down to video quality. The Wired Doorbell Pro records sharper 4K video, and it can automatically respond to visitors with prerecorded messages. The Battery Doorbell Plus has fewer features and can capture video in slightly less sharp 2K resolution. Beyond that, the two doorbells share many of the same core features.  Both can provide a head-to-toe view of your doorstep and support motion detection, two-way talk, and support for color night vision. If you’re willing to pay $4.99 for a monthly subscription , you also get more specific alerts for people, packages, and vehicles. Upgrading to the $19.99 Ring Pro plan, meanwhile, grants access to extra AI features like facial recognition and text-based activity summaries, all of which are free for the first month. Both also work well with Amazon Alexa, allowing you to view a live feed on a compatible Echo Show smart display and receive audible announcements when someone rings your doorbell. ]]> Andrew J. All four colors are currently discounted and available refurbished through the company, with the base 256GB model listed for $599 (usually $699 new), and the upgraded version with 512GB of storage and TouchID selling for $679 (usually $799). The laptops have a one-year manufacturer warranty, with the option to purchase an extended AppleCare plan. MacBook Neo Apple’s most affordable laptop, with a 13-inch display, A18 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, and optional Touch ID fingerprint sensor. Read our review . Where to Buy: $599 at Apple (256GB, Refurbished) My colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto reviewed the MacBook Neo, and was impressed with its performance given that it’s running on the A18 Pro – an iPhone 16 Pro processor. While power users might feel a bit limited by the 8GB of memory and relatively slow storage, the excellent screen, keyboard and speakers make this a great choice for people who primarily use browsers instead of system-intensive apps. It’s also a fantastic laptop for high school or college students. Read our Apple MacBook Neo review . Other deals to consider Amazon has the Google Pixelsnap Charger on sale for $41.99 (usually $69.99), the lowest price we’ve seen yet. This Qi2 wireless charger has a detachable stand to keep your Pixel 10 series phone upright and visible while charging, and supports up to 25W of power for fast charging. It’s worth noting that older Pixel models will need to use a compatible magnet case to attach to the stand. You can pick up a Razer Wolverine V3 Tournament Edition from Amazon for $50, half off its usual price. This wired controller packs in features that competitive gamers will appreciate for tuning in their setup, like remappable back paddles, two trigger heights, and hall effect thumbsticks. It’s compatible with PC and Xbox Series S/X over USB. Fanatical has Steam codes for Peak discounted to $3.75, just over half off its usual price of $7.99. On Monday, the company announced the open-source Treblo AI Music Classifier , which detects when a song was generated using Treblo, though not other AI tools. According to a blog post, it has a false positive rate of less than 1 in 10,000.
